original_question: Which smooth domains have non compact automorphism groups?
target_in_paper: Problem 9.1.1 in Section 9.1 (Automorphisms): "Which smooth domains have non compact automorphism groups?"
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the paper's exact Problem 9.1.1 verbatim and correctly identifies the two core ingredients: smooth domains and non compact automorphism groups.
missing_details: The ambient setting should be stated explicitly: the problem is about domains Ω ⊂ C^n in the several-complex-variables setting of the paper.
If full stand-alone precision is desired, 'domain' means a connected open subset of C^n.
To make the question self-contained, 'smooth domain' should be unpacked as a domain with smooth boundary; the paper itself does not specify a finer smoothness class beyond 'smooth'.
The relevant group is Aut(Ω), the group of biholomorphic self-maps of Ω.
The phrase 'non compact automorphism group' is naturally interpreted using the usual compact-open topology on Aut(Ω) (equivalently, uniform convergence on compact subsets).
The wording 'Which' should be sharpened into an explicit classification/characterization request.
No boundedness, pseudoconvexity, convexity, or finite-type assumption appears in Problem 9.1.1, so a paper-faithful rewrite should not silently add any of these hypotheses.
refined_question: Classify the domains Ω ⊂ C^n with smooth boundary for which the biholomorphic automorphism group Aut(Ω), equipped with its usual compact-open topology, is noncompact.
